sights.w: 1.3-mile waterfront park across six DUMBO/Brooklyn Heights piers with lawns, kayaking and skyline views.
Landmarked 1927 wooden roller coaster at Luna Park, still rattling riders in its 99th season on the boardwalk.
Open-air weekend food market at Marsha P. Johnson State Park with 70+ vendors and Manhattan skyline views.
Historic boardwalk aquarium in Coney Island with sharks, sea otters and a coral reef Ocean Wonders hall.
Six-million-square-foot Sunset Park waterfront complex of food halls, makers, breweries and design studios.
Red Hook nonprofit cultural center fusing visual art, music and science in a restored 19th-century ironworks.
Crown Heights museum founded 1899, the world's first designed for children, with hands-on culture and nature exhibits.
Thirty hillside burial vaults from the 1850s inside Green-Wood Cemetery, opened only for guided tours and concerts.
Free three-floor exhibition center telling the shipbuilding and industrial history of the working Navy Yard.
New York City's oldest structure, a circa-1652 Dutch farmhouse in East Flatbush open for tours Fridays and Saturdays.
1849 Brooklyn Heights church, an abolitionist Underground Railroad stop where Lincoln and Beecher preached against slavery.
Free floating museum aboard the 1914 Lehigh Valley Barge No. 79, moored at Pier 44 in Red Hook.
One-dollar Coney Island USA museum of sideshow memorabilia, vintage arcade games and amusement-district history.

food.w: Cult BYOB Carroll Gardens pizzeria where Mark Iacono cuts dough by wine bottle for a legendary thin pie and calzones.

food.dish: seasonal small plates and natural wine
food.w: Michelin-starred Williamsburg wine bar co-owned by James Murphy, pairing natural wine with chef Nick Curtola's plates.
Williamsburg slice shop famous for its blistered thin crust and a burrata-and-pistachio square that draws long lines.
Red Hook pit house smoking Texas-style brisket, beef ribs and Korean sticky ribs in a cavernous warehouse room.
Missy Robbins's airy Williamsburg trattoria in a former garage, renowned for wood-grilled fish and handmade pasta.
Michelin-listed Palestinian kitchen on Bay Ridge's 3rd Avenue serving musakhan, maqluba and generous mezze spreads.
Brighton Beach refuge for Uyghur and Central Asian cooking, from lamb kebabs to hand-pulled laghman noodles.
Longtime Sheepshead Bay spot near Brighton Beach for Uzbek plov, samsa and steamed manti in a warm dining room.
Crown Heights Trinidadian counter turning out doubles, dhalpuri roti and curry goat on the Nostrand roti corridor.
Cash-only Sunset Park Chinatown takeout for Yunnan crossing-the-bridge noodles assembled in fragrant chicken broth.
Fort Greene Mediterranean spot from chef Tomer Blechman with a leafy garden and modern Israeli seasonal cooking.
DUMBO coal-oven pizzeria from Grimaldi's founder Patsy Grimaldi, under the Brooklyn Bridge and named for his mother.

food.dish: handmade glazed and Bavarian cream doughnuts
food.w: 1950s Greenpoint donut counter beloved for hand-cut glazed rings and cream-filled classics behind a vintage sign.

food.dish: tonkotsu ramen with crispy pork belly
food.w: Prospect Heights ramen-ya from Morimoto alums known for its rich broths and heaping kale-and-sesame salad.
Rustic Bed-Stuy Neapolitan pizzeria and bakery on Lewis Avenue with wood-fired pies and a leafy back patio.

food.dish: cavatelli with sage and brown butter
food.w: Carroll Gardens Italian mainstay with a garden, house cavatelli, crostini and its own cold-pressed olive oil.
Quiet Bushwick corner spot pairing wood-fired naturally-leavened sourdough pizzas with a natural wine list.
Black-owned Bed-Stuy soul food room since 2009 for Nashville hot chicken, shrimp and grits and buttermilk biscuits.
Century-old Atlantic Avenue Middle Eastern grocer on the Cobble Hill border, famous for bulk nuts, olives and spices.
Park Slope bakery-cafe from Michelin-starred chef Daniel Eddy with sourdough bread, pastries and rotisserie plates.
